name: Cartesian Coordinates
description: Describing positions using x, y, and z axes—the most common way to locate things in space.

content.overview: How do you tell someone exactly where something is? Cartesian coordinates are the answer you already know without realizing it—it's just axes on a graph, like the grid on graph paper. You've been using this since grade school! {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Cartesian = position using (x, y) in 2D or (x, y, z) in 3D
The most natural system we've got: horizontal, vertical, and depth
Axes are always perpendicular (90°) to each other
Origin is just wherever the axes cross—your zero point
You'll see it everywhere: maps, graphs, every physics problem you'll ever solve
content.whyItMatters: You're about to use Cartesian coordinates constantly in physics, so it's worth getting comfortable with it now. Every motion problem, every position you plot, every force vector you draw—it all starts by picking a set of axes and locating a point on them. Master this and everything after gets easier.
